claims.statement: The MCP client keeps one Streamable HTTP session on a tokio runtime, reconnecting every three seconds, and turns `resources/list_changed` into the `dataChanged` signal.
Workspace keys are disabled while a terminal widget has focus.
Opening a page navigates the current page tab unless that tab is pinned; otherwise a new tab opens.
Each terminal is a tmux session with titles forwarded; a title that asks for attention raises a desktop notification once per title and at most once a minute.

The look is a set of colour roles from one of three sources: a built-in preset, the Omarchy desktop theme mapped onto the roles, or a TOML file under `~/.config/rusty/themes/`; `skin::tokens` derives every token the shell and the renderer bind to, the older names included, so no binding knows where a colour came from.

The workspace state (sidebars, panes, expanded folders, the graph and page layouts, bookmarks, roots, the skin, the agent pane's session id per page under `agentSessions`, the editing mode under `editMode`) lives in a JSON file the Rust side loads and saves.
Edits autosave one and a half seconds after the last keystroke, in the source editor and in a live-preview section alike, through one timer and one `save`.

The right sidebar's Tags pane lists every tag as a tree with counts, searches by tag on a click or Enter, and tags the open page from a `+` shown on hover, a right-click menu or the `T` key on the keyboard-selected row (the list is focused by a click or by the "Tags: Show tags" command); the tagging goes through the note's own `tagThePage`, and the counts follow the change notification.

The properties block in reading view edits each value by its type through the property tools and adds a key of a chosen type; Tags is among the types, with its key fixed to `tags` and a list value, and a page that already has `tags` gets that row's field focused instead of a second key.

The graph view draws `brain_graph`'s nodes and edges on a `Canvas`, laid out by a force simulation (pairwise repulsion, springs on edges, a pull to the centre, damping and cooling) that runs on a 33 ms timer and stops when the layout settles; its filter, group, display and force settings persist in the workspace state under `graph`.
Ctrl+G, the ribbon button and the palette open the global graph as one tab; "Open local graph" on a page opens one local graph tab that follows the last page that was current.

Bookmarks are one JSON array under `bookmarks` in the workspace state, entries of kind file, folder, search or heading with a title; adding one that exists removes it; opening one navigates to the page, reveals the folder, runs the search, or scrolls to the heading once the page has rendered.

The search pane sends the query as typed with `case_sensitive` and `regex` from its two chips and bookmarks the search from a third; Settings renders the palette's command list as the Hotkeys table, the terminal keys added, behind a filter field.

The skin choice (`source`, `name`, `scanlines`) lives under `theme` in the workspace state; a pick in Settings goes through `selectTheme`, which stores it and calls `Theme.select` so every token repaints at once, while the application font is set from the saved skin before the engine loads, so a face change applies at the next launch.

The top bar reads the machine through `Desk` (memory in use, the CPU's share since the last reading, the clock, refreshed every two seconds) and carries the command button and one glyph per agent CLI found on the machine: a click opens the agent in a new tab, a right-click opens the agent pane, both as signals the window answers; the Hyprland workspace strip is gone and `Desk` no longer asks the compositor for anything.

The theme carries a base text size (`baseSize`, 12 to 18, default 14, or `RUSTY_TEXT_SIZE` when set, which then wins) and `scale` (`baseSize / 12`); every QML text size is `Math.round(n * theme.scale)` where `n` is the drawn pixel value, the reading view's render style takes its `size` from the same scale and re-renders on a change, and the terminal keeps the Alacritty font at a fixed point size.

The base text size lives as `textSize` in the workspace state, is applied at load, and is set through the window's `setTextSize` by Ctrl with plus, minus and zero (outside a terminal), by three palette commands, and by a stepper under "This machine" in Settings; a Rust test refuses any literal `pixelSize` in the QML and any literal `pointSize` outside the terminal.

The file and folder bookmarks are the favorites: the note header shows a star that toggles the open page's bookmark (Ctrl+D and a palette command do the same), the explorer gathers them in a Favorites section above the tree where a click opens and a right-click removes, and the quick switcher lists them first and starred on an empty query; nothing new is stored.

The Secrets page masks every value, offers to set a PIN when the server reports none, unlocks through `secret_unlock` and keeps the token in the page's memory alone, reveals one row at a time through `secret_reveal`, saves an inline edit on Enter through `secret_update`, copies through a hidden text editor, and relocks on the expiry the unlock answered, on window focus loss, on Lock and whenever a reveal or update fails; `pin_timeout_minutes` is among the known settings.

The explorer lists folders from the machine below the vault tree as roots kept per machine under `roots` in the workspace state (added through a folder picker, removed from their menu, expansion under the same `expanded` map keyed by absolute path); the disk is read by the app's `Folders` type (a cached listing with folders first and dotfiles skipped, a kind by extension then a sniff of the first eight kilobytes, text up to a megabyte, `xdg-open`), never through the back end; a file opens in a `file` tab (markdown rendered by `brain_render` given the text with a Source toggle, text as numbered monospace lines, an image fitted) or, for any other kind, through the desktop; a folder's menu opens one terminal tab per installed agent or a shell with that folder as the working directory, copies the path, reveals it, refreshes the listing; links, backlinks, graph and search never see the roots.

The Decisions view (a tab opened from the ribbon, the palette or `openView("decisions")`) is fed by `brain_due` alone: the follow-ups due first, then every decision with its status and dates, a click opening the page; the graph view draws a decision's typed edges (`kind` other than `link`) dashed in the accent colour behind a "Decision edges" filter kept with the other graph settings.

The app binary doubles as the command front end: `rusty <name>` checks the active skills store for a matching script before Qt starts and, on a hit, execs `rusty-cli scripts run` in place of opening the window, so no GUI is created for a command invocation.
The Skills tab carries a Scripts section beside the skill list, reading `script_list` and `script_view` and saving through `script_update`, so a script is edited where its skill is.

A terminal's clipboard is bound on the widget itself: Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+Shift+V call the exported `copyClipboard` and `pasteClipboard`, attached with `Keys.priority: BeforeItem` so they run before the widget's own key handling and plain Ctrl+C stays the shell's interrupt; a `TapHandler` accepting only the middle and right buttons pastes the primary selection (`pasteSelection`) or opens a Copy/Paste menu, taking an exclusive grab (`ReleaseWithinBounds`) so the widget's native middle-click paste cannot fire a second time and a left-button drag still selects; the menu's Copy is enabled by the widget's `copyAvailable` signal, read through `Connections { ignoreUnknownSignals: true }`.

The sidebar splitters are two instances of the shared `Splitter.qml`, which measures a drag in scene coordinates (`mapToItem(null, …)` at press and at every move) rather than in its own frame, because the pane resize moves the handle under the pointer and a delta measured from it would be measured from a moving origin; each call site binds `value`, `min` and `max` (180–600 left, 200–700 right, the right one `invert`ed so a drag left grows it) and writes the width in `onMoved`, and the widths persist in the workspace state.

Document tabs reorder by drag: a `DragHandler` on each tab (left button, x axis only, no target of its own) records the origin when it activates and, when it releases, maps its centroid into the tab row, finds the tab whose span holds that x (`dropIndexAt`, which skips the row's spacer and `+` because only delegates carry an `index`), and calls the same `moveTab` the Ctrl+Shift+PgUp/PgDown keys and the tab menu use, so the order persists as it already did; the tab's tap handlers are untouched, and a press that becomes a drag never fires a select.

The tab strip's `+` opens a menu under itself: the page switcher first (what the `+` always opened; Ctrl+T is unchanged), then one item per agent CLI the top bar lists (`win.agents`, built by an `Instantiator` inserted between two separators, because a `Repeater` does not parent items into a `Menu`) that opens that agent in a new terminal tab, then the custom terminal dialog (Ctrl+Shift+T, unchanged); its tooltip names both keys.

The rename-tab dialog lays its field out in a `ColumnLayout` with a preferred width, the shape the new-terminal dialog uses, because a bare child with an explicit `width` does not size a `Dialog`'s content and the field spilled past the dialog's right edge.

Screenshot scenes exist for the chrome that only shows on demand: `RUSTY_SHOT_SCENE=rename` opens the rename dialog for the current tab, `plus` pops the tab strip's menu, `skills:collapse-scripts` (or `collapse-skills`) sets the Skills page's remembered layout before `view:skills` opens it, `file:<path>` opens a file tab and `file:edit` puts it in edit mode, `root:<path>` adds a folder root and expands it once the roots have changed, `expand:<path>` opens any row, `tagfield:<text>` puts the text in the open page's tags field so the completion list shows, `agent:ask:<text>` shows the agent pane and sends the text (the screenshot script points `RUSTY_CLAUDE_BIN` at a fake `claude` it seeds), `import:<path>` opens the import dialog with the plan for a vault (the script seeds a small one), `live:<n>` puts the open page in live preview with section n open — a scene path is taken as given when absolute and under `HOME` otherwise — so each can be photographed offscreen against a scratch vault.

`Splitter.qml` is the one drag handle in the module, listed in `build.rs` and shared by the sidebars and the Skills page: the owner binds `value`, `min`, `max` and `invert` and applies the result in `onMoved`; the handle clamps and reports but never writes a value itself, which is what lets one component serve a window pane and a page.

The Skills page's list pane is resizable through a `Splitter` clamped 200–600 px, and its Skills and Scripts sections collapse from focusable headers (a chevron and a label; click, or Enter and Space when focused) with the open section taking the freed height; the split and both open states travel as one JSON string — `savedLayout` in, `layoutChanged` out, guarded against echo while applying — kept as `ui.skillsLayout` in the workspace state the way `graph` and `bookmarks` are.

The explorer's disk writes (new file, new folder, rename, move, delete) go through six `Folders` invokables that answer `{ok, path}` or `{ok, error}`: every write refuses an existing target, a name that is empty, a slash, `.` or `..` is refused before the disk is touched, delete moves the entry to the XDG home trash (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/Trash`, else `~/.local/share/Trash`) under `files/` with its `.trashinfo` record written first and a copy-then-remove across devices, and on `ok` the explorer drops the root's listing cache and rebuilds while an error shows in its notice and changes nothing else.

A disk file or folder moves by a vertical `DragHandler` on its row (no target of its own) released over a `dir` or `root` row under the same root — never across roots, never onto the vault, a drop on its own folder a no-op — or by Move to… from its menu; F2 renames inline and Delete opens the delete dialog for disk and vault rows alike, the dialog naming the trash for a disk row and `archive/` for a vault row.

A text or markdown file tab has an edit mode: a `TextArea` in the terminal face without a highlighter, a dirty mark in the header, a save through `write_text` one and a half seconds after the last keystroke and on Ctrl+S (a sibling temporary file renamed over the path, the mode kept, so a crash leaves the old file whole), Reload refused with a notice while dirty, and a markdown re-render after a save.

A folder root's git status is read by the app's `Folders` type and never written: `git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel` then `status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=all -- .` in the root, parsed in Rust into `{repo, branch, files, dirs}` with paths relative to the root (a root that is a subfolder sees only its subtree) and every folder above a change folded to the strongest state below it (M over A over ?); the explorer fetches it once per root in `rebuild`, keeps it beside the listing cache and drops both on Refresh, a root change and every disk write, and rows only read it — the letter on a file, a dot on a folder, the branch on the root, in the `gold`, `alive`, `accentSoft` and `faint` tokens; outside a repository or without `git` the answer is `{repo:false}` and the tree is unmarked.

Tagging a page deliberately is one writer, `NoteTab.tagThePage` (a leading `#` dropped, a duplicate refused without case, a scalar `tags:` counted as one tag, then `brain_set_property` on `tags`), reached from the tags row's field, the Tags pane and the palette; the tags row's field completes from the tag index the window already holds (`win.tags`, re-read on every change notification): a substring match without case, the page's own tags left out, ranked by count then name, eight at most, nothing picked until Down, Enter adding the text as typed when nothing is picked, Tab taking the pick or the first; "Tags: Tag this page" focuses that field, adding the `tags` property first when the page has none and focusing the new row once the re-render creates it.

The agent pane is a headless Claude Code, not a terminal: the app's `Assistant` type spawns `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose --permission-prompt-tool stdio --permission-mode default --strict-mcp-config` with Rusty's own server as an HTTP MCP server, its read-only tools pre-allowed by name (`READ_TOOLS`), the open page named in `--append-system-prompt`, `HOME` as the working directory, and `--resume <id>` when the page has a session; a reader thread hands each stdout line to the Qt thread, where `parse_line` turns it into typed signals (init, block start, text delta and final text, tool input, tool result, permission asked, turn done, notice, exit) that the pane renders as items of its own — selectable text, a tool call with its input, its result in the terminal face, a permission prompt whose Allow or Deny writes a `control_response`, a notice; Enter sends a `user` message, Stop sends an `interrupt` control request, an exit is reported with the tail of stderr and any message restarts; a session id comes from the `init` event into `ui.agentSessions` and an exit before `init` forgets a stale one; the terminal tabs stay tmux terminals, Codex has no print mode so the pane is Claude-only and says when `claude` is missing.

Importing an Obsidian vault from the app is a palette command ("Vault: Import an Obsidian vault…") that opens a folder picker, then `importDialog`, which asks `brain_import_plan` and shows the summary and the details (pages, attachments, collisions, unresolved links, tags, bookmarks kept and not carried) before anything is written; Import asks `brain_import`, and the answer's bookmarks are merged into `ui.bookmarks` through `bookmarkIndex` in the app's own shapes (file, folder, search, heading), the tree, pages and tags refresh, and the dialog shows what came in and the report page's slug.

Sources reach the app through two palette commands — "Sources: Capture a URL…" opens `captureDialog`, whose URL goes to `source_capture` and whose answer opens the new page (a failed capture is named in the notice), and "Sources: Search sources" runs the `type:source` search — and a page under `sources/` shows a glyph of its own (`⌁`, in the faint token) in the explorer's tree and its type and `url` in its properties; the screenshot script seeds one such page for the `open:sources/…` scene and maps the `reading` scene alone to the empty scene by an exact match.

A page has three views: reading, live preview and source. Live preview is the default editing mode (`ui.editMode`, `live` or `source`, per the user): the reading view's blocks stay rendered and a click on one (not on a link) opens that section alone as a highlighted source editor, the caret on the line the click's height points at; the page is split into parts by `page_sections` in Rust (the frontmatter, then one part per heading line outside fenced code, joined back byte for byte, tested) reached through `Tools.pageSections`, and the parts line up with the renderer's `HEADING_MARK` blocks one to one; when they do not, live preview edits the whole body in the source editor rather than guess; a save assembles the page from the parts with the open section's text in place; while a section is open the page is not re-rendered (a save's answer and a change notification wait) and committing it (Escape, a click elsewhere, leaving edit mode) renders again; `Ctrl+E` and the header toggle reading against the user's mode, "View: Reading view", "View: Live preview" and "View: Source mode" set it, and the header reads `[ READ ]`, `[ LIVE ]` or `[ EDIT ]`.
